summary: Adapts gendered German spellings locally in the browser to personal reading preferences – without tracking, telemetry or cloud services.
description:
Sprachverstand processes German-language website text directly in the browser. Forms such as Nutzer:innen, Mitarbeiter*innen, NutzerInnen, paired forms and selected participle forms can be adapted using controlled, configurable rules.

German is a complex language. Sprachverstand therefore works deliberately cautiously: unknown or ambiguous forms remain unchanged when a sufficiently reliable replacement is not possible. Missing or problematic cases can be reported on GitHub.

Features include personal exceptions and custom literal replacements, domain exclusions, processing of dynamically loaded content, and optional handling of subtitles and accessible labels. Settings can be backed up and restored locally as JSON. Selected settings categories can optionally be synchronized through Firefox Sync; this feature is disabled by default.

Website text is not transmitted to the developer or to external language services. Sprachverstand uses no proprietary cloud, tracking, telemetry, advertising or user profiles. When Firefox synchronization is enabled, only the explicitly selected settings data is transmitted through the browser's synchronization service.

The website and its server-side data remain unchanged. When Sprachverstand is disabled, local changes on open pages are reverted without reloading.

Sprachverstand does not tell anyone how texts should be written. It gives users control over how German-language text is displayed and read aloud on their own device.
